latest_teacher_action.diagnosis: The previous prompt preserved object presence, colors, and the koalas-in-front relation, but it was too loose for exact counting of the six trumpets and five giraffes. 'Arranged behind them' and 'a separate visible group to the side' encouraged grouped or partially merged objects, making trumpet and giraffe instances hard to count distinctly. The retry should use stricter row-based layout, wider separation, full visibility, and explicit anti-merge language for the failed count targets while preserving the already-correct koalas, colors, and front/behind relation.
expected_improvement: Increase detector confidence for exactly six trumpets by placing all six as separate, fully visible pink instruments in one clear back row.
Increase detector confidence for exactly five giraffes by placing all five as separate, fully visible brown animals in one clear side row.
Preserve the already-passing four yellow koalas and their position in front of the trumpets while reducing overlap that could hide the trumpets.
preserve_constraints: The four yellow koalas are in front of the trumpets.
Koalas, trumpets, and giraffes are all present.

previous_plan_error.details: The plan used general separation language but did not enforce a simple count-friendly composition for the trumpets and giraffes. It allowed the failed object groups to appear as clustered, overlapping, or partially hidden instead of as individually countable instances.

latest_teacher_action.regeneration_strategy: Use a simple wide composition with three clearly separated groups: six pink trumpets in a single fully visible back row, four yellow koalas in a single front row directly in front of the trumpets with minimal overlap, and five brown giraffes in a separate single side row. Make every instance complete, evenly spaced, and visually separable. Add explicit negatives against extra instances and against merged, cropped, stacked, or hidden objects.
regression_risks: Making the trumpets too small or too occluded behind the koalas could break the trumpet count again.
Crowding all three groups into one area could cause giraffes to merge visually and hurt the giraffe count.
Changing layout too aggressively could regress the passed relation that koalas are in front of the trumpets.
repair_constraints: Show exactly six pink trumpets, all fully visible and individually countable, arranged in one horizontal back row behind the koalas.
Show exactly five brown giraffes, all fully visible and individually countable, arranged in one separate horizontal row to one side of the koalas and trumpets.
Keep wide spacing between each trumpet and between each giraffe so no two instances touch, overlap, merge, or hide each other.
Keep the four yellow koalas in front of the trumpets, but leave enough open space so each of the six trumpets remains visible behind them.
Do not include any extra trumpets or extra giraffes.

retry_ready_action.diagnosis: The previous prompt preserved object presence, colors, and the koalas-in-front relation, but it was too loose for exact counting of the six trumpets and five giraffes. 'Arranged behind them' and 'a separate visible group to the side' encouraged grouped or partially merged objects, making trumpet and giraffe instances hard to count distinctly. The retry should use stricter row-based layout, wider separation, full visibility, and explicit anti-merge language for the failed count targets while preserving the already-correct koalas, colors, and front/behind relation.
expected_improvement: Increase detector confidence for exactly six trumpets by placing all six as separate, fully visible pink instruments in one clear back row.
Increase detector confidence for exactly five giraffes by placing all five as separate, fully visible brown animals in one clear side row.
Preserve the already-passing four yellow koalas and their position in front of the trumpets while reducing overlap that could hide the trumpets.

previous_plan_error.details: The plan used general separation language but did not enforce a simple count-friendly composition for the trumpets and giraffes. It allowed the failed object groups to appear as clustered, overlapping, or partially hidden instead of as individually countable instances.

retry_ready_action.regeneration_strategy: Use a simple wide composition with three clearly separated groups: six pink trumpets in a single fully visible back row, four yellow koalas in a single front row directly in front of the trumpets with minimal overlap, and five brown giraffes in a separate single side row. Make every instance complete, evenly spaced, and visually separable. Add explicit negatives against extra instances and against merged, cropped, stacked, or hidden objects.
regression_risks: Making the trumpets too small or too occluded behind the koalas could break the trumpet count again.
Crowding all three groups into one area could cause giraffes to merge visually and hurt the giraffe count.
Changing layout too aggressively could regress the passed relation that koalas are in front of the trumpets.
repair_constraints: Show exactly six pink trumpets, all fully visible and individually countable, arranged in one horizontal back row behind the koalas.
Show exactly five brown giraffes, all fully visible and individually countable, arranged in one separate horizontal row to one side of the koalas and trumpets.
Keep wide spacing between each trumpet and between each giraffe so no two instances touch, overlap, merge, or hide each other.
Keep the four yellow koalas in front of the trumpets, but leave enough open space so each of the six trumpets remains visible behind them.
Do not include any extra trumpets or extra giraffes.
